subject: Geography
description: Major Indian national parks — Jim Corbett, Kaziranga, Gir, Ranthambore, Sundarbans, Periyar, Bandipur; flagship species, states.

questions.stem: JIM CORBETT NATIONAL PARK, India's first national park, is located in:
questions.explanation: JIM CORBETT NATIONAL PARK — INDIA'S FIRST national park, established 1936 as 'Hailey National Park' (after then-Governor of UP Sir Malcolm Hailey). RENAMED to JIM CORBETT (1957) after the legendary British-Indian hunter-turned-conservationist who single-handedly stopped several man-eating tigers in the area, then became wildlife photographer/author ('Man-eaters of Kumaon'). LOCATION: NAINITAL + Pauri Garhwal districts, UTTARAKHAND. AREA: ~520 sq km core; ~1,300 sq km tiger reserve. FAUNA: ~250 BENGAL TIGERS (one of highest densities in India); leopard, elephant, sambar, chital, gharial, mahseer fish (in Ramganga river). FIRST 'PROJECT TIGER' RESERVE — 1973 (along with Bandipur, Kanha, Manas, Melghat, Palamau, Ranthambore, Simlipal, Sundarbans). RAMGANGA RIVER flows through. Visited by hundreds of thousands of tourists yearly. PROJECT TIGER stats (current): ~3,167 tigers in India (2022 census, ~71% of world's wild tigers), up from ~1,400 in 2006. INDIA'S FIRST NATIONAL PARK chronology: (1) Jim Corbett 1936. (2) Kanha NP 1955. (3) Tadoba 1955. (4) Sundarbans 1984. (5) Many more in 1980s-90s. PYQ FREQUENCY: Corbett-first-NP fact in SSC GA, UPSC, NDA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: KAZIRANGA NATIONAL PARK is famous for which UNESCO-listed flagship species?
questions.explanation: KAZIRANGA NATIONAL PARK (Assam, ~430 sq km in core, ~1,000 sq km in greater Kaziranga). UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985). FLAGSHIP: GREAT INDIAN ONE-HORNED RHINOCEROS (Rhinoceros unicornis). Population: ~2,613 rhinos as per 2022 census — ~70% of WORLD'S population of this species. CONSERVATION SUCCESS: in 1900s, only ~12 rhinos left in Assam due to poaching for horn (used in Vietnamese/Chinese traditional medicine). Strict protection brought them back. ALSO HOSTS: Asian elephant, swamp deer (barasingha), water buffalo, Bengal tiger (~120 — highest density anywhere!), Hoolock gibbon, ~480 bird species. LANDSCAPE: alluvial floodplains of BRAHMAPUTRA river; tall elephant grass + marshes. PROBLEMS: (1) ANNUAL FLOODS — Brahmaputra inundates ~80% of park (June-September); animals drown or move to highways (vehicle collisions). (2) POACHING — though declining; horn smuggling remains. CONSERVATION TIMELINE: 1908 declared Reserve Forest by Curzon's wife Mary Curzon (after she heard about rhino disappearance); 1916 game sanctuary; 1974 NP. RHINO POPULATIONS in INDIA: Kaziranga (~2,600), Manas NP (~50, recovering), Pobitora WS (~100, highest density per area), Orang NP, Dudhwa (UP). PYQ FREQUENCY: Kaziranga-rhino in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: GIR NATIONAL PARK is the only HOME of which big cat species in India?
questions.explanation: GIR NATIONAL PARK (Junagadh, GUJARAT) — ~258 sq km core; ~1,400 sq km wildlife sanctuary. THE ONLY home of ASIATIC LION (Panthera leo persica) in INDIA — and indeed in the WILD globally (besides a few in Africa as African lion subspecies). POPULATION: ~675 lions (2020 census); up from ~12 in 1907 — incredible conservation comeback under the Nawabs of Junagadh and later Indian govt. ASIATIC vs AFRICAN LION: Asiatic slightly smaller, has folds of skin on belly (rare in African); MANES less prominent in Asiatic males (ears visible). HISTORY: lions once roamed across N. Africa, Middle East, Persia, India. By 1900s, only Gir remained. IUCN: Asiatic lion classified as ENDANGERED. CONSERVATION CHALLENGES: (1) Single-population RISK — disease (canine distemper killed 24 lions in 2018) could wipe them out. (2) Translocation to KUNO NATIONAL PARK (MP) was approved by SC 2013, but Gujarat resisted. KUNO eventually became home to AFRICAN CHEETAHS reintroduced in 2022. (3) Human-wildlife conflict — Maldhari pastoralists share habitat. ASIATIC LION SUBSPECIES status: classified as Panthera leo persica until 2017; now considered same as Panthera leo leo (Asiatic-North African subspecies). PYQ FREQUENCY: Gir-Lion in SSC, UPSC, NDA — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: SUNDARBANS, the world's largest mangrove forest, is located in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: SUNDARBANS — WORLD'S LARGEST MANGROVE forest. Spans WEST BENGAL (India) + Khulna (BANGLADESH); total ~10,000 sq km, of which ~4,260 sq km in INDIA. Indian portion: SUNDARBANS NATIONAL PARK (1984), tiger reserve, biosphere reserve, UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITE (1987). NAME: 'Sundarbans' = 'beautiful forest' in Bengali (or possibly named after SUNDARI tree, Heritiera fomes — dominant mangrove species). HABITAT: complex network of tidal channels, mudflats, mangrove islands at the GANGA-BRAHMAPUTRA delta. FLAGSHIP: ROYAL BENGAL TIGER — UNIQUE 'SWIMMING TIGERS' that hunt in waist-deep water and prey on aquatic creatures; ~96 tigers in Indian portion. Famous for MAN-EATING incidents (~50 humans killed by tigers each year historically; now declining with conservation/awareness). OTHER SPECIES: estuarine crocodile, gharial, water monitor, Olive Ridley turtle, dolphins. CYCLONES: Sundarbans is regularly battered by Bay of Bengal cyclones (Aila 2009, Bulbul 2019, Amphan 2020) — mangroves provide CRUCIAL STORM PROTECTION for both coastlines. CLIMATE CHANGE: rising sea level threatens to submerge much of Sundarbans by 2100; some islands already lost (Lohachara, Bedford). PYQ FREQUENCY: Sundarbans in SSC, UPSC, NDA, NEET environment — 1-2× per cycle.

questions.stem: RANTHAMBORE NATIONAL PARK, famous for tiger sightings, is in which state?
questions.explanation: RANTHAMBORE NATIONAL PARK — Sawai Madhopur district, RAJASTHAN. Area: ~392 sq km core; ~1,400 sq km tiger reserve. TIGER POPULATION: ~75-80 (2022 census). FAMOUS FOR: (1) Spectacular RANTHAMBORE FORT inside the park — 10th-century AD; UNESCO Heritage. (2) MACHHALI THE TIGRESS (~1996-2016) — the most photographed tiger in the world; lived ~20 years; gave birth to 11 cubs, contributing significantly to RECOVERY of Indian tiger population. (3) Easy tiger sightings due to OPEN, semi-arid terrain (different from dense forests of Sundarbans/Manas). LANDSCAPE: dry deciduous forest + grasslands + lakes (Padam Talao). FAUNA: Bengal tiger, leopard, sloth bear, sambar, chital, blackbuck, mugger crocodile. ONE OF FIRST 9 PROJECT TIGER reserves (1973). KEY CONSERVATION: 'BUFFER ZONE' management, anti-poaching patrols, eco-tourism. RECENT CONCERNS: tiger MORTALITY due to occasional in-fighting + dispersal pressures. RANTHAMBORE is paired with KEOLADEO GHANA NP (Bharatpur, Rajasthan — UNESCO 1985, formerly bird sanctuary), TAL CHHAPAR (blackbuck sanctuary), DESERT NP (Jaisalmer area). RAJASTHAN's TIGER STATUS: ~88 tigers across Ranthambore, Sariska, Mukundra Hills (2022). PYQ FREQUENCY: Ranthambore-Rajasthan in SSC, UPSC, KAS — 1× per cycle.

questions.stem: PERIYAR NATIONAL PARK, famous for its boat safari and elephants, is in which state?
questions.explanation: PERIYAR NATIONAL PARK — IDUKKI district, KERALA, in the Western Ghats. Core area: ~305 sq km; total tiger reserve: ~925 sq km. SPECIAL FEATURE: PERIYAR LAKE (artificial, formed by 1895 dam by British) lies INSIDE the park — visitors can take BOAT SAFARIS to spot wildlife along banks. FLAGSHIP: ASIAN ELEPHANT (Periyar has ~1,000 elephants — one of largest populations in S. India). Also Bengal tiger (~40), gaur (Indian bison), sambar deer, langur, lion-tailed macaque (endangered, endemic to W. Ghats). UNIQUE SPECIES: Nilgiri tahr (mountain goat, endemic to S. India W. Ghats). NEELAKURINJI flowers (Strobilanthes kunthiana) bloom every 12 YEARS — last big bloom 2018. PROJECT TIGER reserve (1978). LOCATION: ~190 km from Kochi airport; popular among S. Indian tourists. NEAR THEKKADY town. WESTERN GHATS — UNESCO Natural Heritage Site (2012); covers 39 sites, biodiversity hotspot, ~30% of India's flora and ~35% of fauna. KERALA WILDLIFE: also Wayanad WS, Silent Valley NP (Mathikettan Shola), Eravikulam NP (Munnar, where Neelakurinji blooms). PYQ FREQUENCY: Periyar-Kerala in SSC, UPSC, NDA 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests state-park associations.

questions.stem: Which national park became HOME to AFRICAN CHEETAHS reintroduced to India in 2022?
questions.explanation: KUNO NATIONAL PARK (Sheopur district, MADHYA PRADESH) — became home to AFRICAN CHEETAHS reintroduced under PROJECT CHEETAH on 17 SEPTEMBER 2022 (PM Modi's birthday). FIRST BATCH: 8 cheetahs from Namibia (5 females + 3 males), released in special soft-release enclosures. SECOND BATCH (Feb 2023): 12 cheetahs from South Africa. CONTEXT: ASIATIC CHEETAH was DECLARED EXTINCT in India in 1952 (last 3 shot by Maharaja Ramanuj Pratap Singh of Korea, Chhattisgarh in 1947). African cheetahs are a different sub-species; introduced as 'free-living' for first time outside Africa. STATUS as of late 2024: ~25 cheetahs alive (incl. cubs born in India). MORTALITY: several cheetahs died (organ failure, infections, fights) — sparking criticism. ORIGINAL PLAN for KUNO: was supposed to be SECOND HOME for ASIATIC LIONS (Gir-only) per SC 2013 order; Gujarat resisted; eventually cheetahs were chosen instead. KUNO LANDSCAPE: dry deciduous forest, grasslands — similar to African savanna habitat. WATCHED: 'Sasha' (first cheetah to die in India, March 2023, kidney issue); 'Asha' (gave birth in 2023). RELATED: African vs Asiatic cheetah are genetically separate subspecies (Acinonyx jubatus jubatus vs A. j. venaticus). PYQ FREQUENCY: Project Cheetah is current-affairs but appears in PT 2024-26.
